# dsh-net-dashboard
A **live network inspection dashboard** in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar: interfaces and IP/MAC, traf
fic rates, TCP/UDP sessions, and latency curves, all read from this machine at request time and refr
eshed every 3 seconds.
English | 中文
## What it does
The panel sits under the built-in sidebar rows and shows the current machine's network quality. It i
s key-first: a KPI strip and four cards, each collapsed to its essentials with a **详情 (Details)** di
st: a KPI strip and four cards, each collapsed to its essentials with a **详情 (Details)** disclosure.
- **KPI strip** — download rate, upload rate, gateway latency and TCP session count, always visible.
- **Live traffic** — aggregate download/upload rates (loopback excluded) with rolling curves and pe

aks. *Details* adds per-interface rates and cumulative in/out counters.
- **Latency** — one compact
row per target: current value, loss chip and a 1-second-resolution mini curve. The default gateway i
s always followed; a public target is configurable. *Details* adds average / min / max / jitter / lo

ss / received-sent statistics.
- **Sessions** — TCP session total, UDP socket count and the top stat

e bars. *Details* adds the full TCP state breakdown and a session-count trend.
- **Network** — prima
ry interface with IPv4, gateway, DNS resolvers and public IP at a glance. *Details* adds IPv6, MAC,
Wi-Fi facts, hostname, OS version and a full interface table with live per-interface rates.
| Dark theme | Expanded details |
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use `--profile web` for the browser profile. The Web **Plugins** page and the `plugin_manager` tool
accept the same address. The plugin ships plain JavaScript — no build step, no dependencies.
## How it works
The host half (`lib/index.js`) mounts one loopback-only route, `GET /api/net-dashboard/snapshot`:
- Each request runs `ifconfig`, `route`, `netstat` and `scutil --dns` (all bounded), plus `ipconfig

getsummary` for Wi-Fi facts.
- Traffic rates come from diffing `netstat -ib` byte counters against t

he previous sample held in memory.
- Latency is fed by persistent `ping -i 1` child processes (one p
er target, restarted on failure, stopped with the plugin) into a rolling window; the route only read

s that window, so a 3-second poll never spawns command storms.
- The public IP lookup is cached for
10 minutes and can be disabled.
The browser half (`lib/client.js`) polls the snapshot every 3 seconds (toggleable, persisted in `loc
alStorage`), keeps its own rolling history for the traffic and session curves, and draws every chart
as inline SVG — no chart dependency. Colors use the shell theme tokens, so light and dark themes bo
ne SVG — no chart dependency. Colors use the shell theme tokens, so light and dark themes both work.
## Routes
| Route | Method | Purpose |
| `api/net-dashboard/snapshot` | GET | one full snapshot: interfaces, primary facts, traffic, sessio
shboard/snapshot` | GET | one full snapshot: interfaces, primary facts, traffic, sessions, latency |
The route sits behind a loopback-only trust fence (loopback socket **and** loopback Host header, sam
e-origin markers enforced); paired remote devices are rejected.
## Configuration
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | set `false` to mount nothing |
| `pingTargets` | `["223.5.5.5"]` | extra late

ncy targets; the default gateway is always followed |
| `publicIp` | `true` | enable the cached publ

he default gateway is always followed |
| `publicIp` | `true` | enable the cached public IP lookup |
## Requirements and limitations

- The collector commands and parsers target **macOS**.
- Without Location permission macOS hides Wi-

Fi SSID/RSSI; those rows are simply omitted.
- Traffic rates need two snapshots to materialize, so t
he first poll shows `—`.
